paragraphs.source_en: On the morning of the seventeenth day of the third month of Tenshō 12, Tokugawa Ieyasu recalled Sakai Saemon-no-jō Tadatsugu, whom he had sent to Kuwana. The two rode side by side up to the position on Mount Komaki, whereupon Ieyasu immediately summoned his staff to council.

units.source_en: On the morning of the seventeenth day of the third month of Tenshō 12, Tokugawa Ieyasu recalled Sakai Saemon-no-jō Tadatsugu, whom he had sent to Kuwana. The two rode side by side up to the position on Mount Komaki, whereupon Ieyasu immediately summoned his staff to council.
units.source_zh: 天正十二年三月十七晨，德川家康把已派往桑名的酒井左卫门尉忠次召回，与其并辔登上小牧山的阵地，随后立刻把幕僚们召集起来议事。

paragraphs.source_zh: 天正十二年三月十七晨，德川家康把已派往桑名的酒井左卫门尉忠次召回，与其并辔登上小牧山的阵地，随后立刻把幕僚们召集起来议事。

paragraphs.source_en: Those present included Honda Heihachirō Tadakatsu, who was staunchly guarding the position on Mount Komaki’s southern slope; Ishikawa Hōki-no-kami Kazumasa on the mountain itself; Sakakibara Koheita Yasumasa, who had secretly slipped north to reconnoiter the enemy; Okudaira Nobumasa and Ii Manchiyo Naomasa, stationed at Negoya to the northeast; and Nobukatsu’s commander Amano Kagetoshi, among others. Wiping the sweat from their brows, they discussed the state of the war.

paragraphs.source_en: As Okudaira’s vanguard advanced abreast of Sakakibara’s troops, the enemy ahead suddenly raised a clamor. In moments they formed a single column and bore down upon Yasumasa.

paragraphs.source_en: When he learned that Nabeta Kurando-no-jō, commander of the vanguard, had been shot dead, Mori Musashi-no-kami Nagayoshi flew into a towering rage. At the time he was commanding the main camp at Hachimanbayashi, planning to divide his army into three columns and drive the enemy back to Komaki in a single rush. With Kurando-no-jō dead, however, he had no choice but to alter his battle plan.

paragraphs.source_en: “Very well, Sakakibara Yasumasa—I shall fight you to the death!” Eyes blazing with fury, Mori Nagayoshi laughed wildly at the double-flowered cherry trees whose blossoms had not yet entirely fallen.

units.source_en: “Very well, Sakakibara Yasumasa—I shall fight you to the death!”
units.source_zh: “好，神原康政，我跟你拼了！”

units.source_en: Eyes blazing with fury, Mori Nagayoshi laughed wildly at the double-flowered cherry trees whose blossoms had not yet entirely fallen.

paragraphs.source_en: By then Mori Nagayoshi had received another report: Hideyoshi’s two generals, Horio Mosuke and Yamauchi Inosuke, had been ordered by Hideyoshi to enter Haguro shortly. The young Musashi-no-kami was deeply displeased. He and his brother Ranmaru had lost their father at an early age, and both were fiercely determined to outdo others. Before Horio and Yamauchi could enter Haguro, he was determined to seize the initiative and secure victory firmly in his own hands.

paragraphs.source_en: The blast of conch horns shattered the springtime stillness, while banners of every color fluttered along both sides of the road.

To the enemy, it must have seemed that Sakakibara Yasumasa had been so terrified by the renowned “Devil Musashi” that he was fleeing with his tail between his legs.
